Gutter guards in Melbourne

Guards change the interval. They do not end it.

Anyone selling you a gutter guard as the last gutter job you will ever need is selling you something. A good mesh keeps leaf and bark out of the channel, which on a house under a gum is worth real money. Fine debris still gets through, and leaf still sits on top of the mesh and has to come off.

  • An honest answer about whether yours is worth it
  • Priced per linear metre, fitted
  • Maintenance reduced, not removed
Get A Quote 0400 638 010
  1. Home
  2. Services
  3. Windows, gutters, roof and solar
  4. Gutter guards

What a guard actually does

It stops the bulk material getting into the gutter: gum leaves, bark strips, twigs, seed pods, the things that physically pack a channel and stop it draining. On a house under a eucalypt that is most of the problem, and solving it is genuinely valuable.

What it does not do is keep the gutter clean. Fine debris, roof grit and the windblown dust that becomes black silt all pass through any mesh fine enough to still let water in. And whatever lands on top of the mesh stays there, where it eventually mats down, holds water and becomes its own small ecosystem. The gutter still gets inspected and the mesh still gets cleared. Just less often.

Is it worth it on your house

An honest decision table

We fit guards and we also talk people out of them. Both happen regularly.

What we would actually say, depending on what is above your roof.
  Our honest view Why
Gum or plane trees directly overhanging Yes, clearly worth it You are currently paying for two cleans a year and still getting blockages between them
Large trees nearby but not overhanging Probably worth it Wind carries enough in to pack a gutter over a season
Open block, no trees close by Probably not A guard will not pay for itself against a clean every two years
A roof you cannot safely access Yes, on safety grounds alone Reducing how often anyone has to be up there is the real benefit
Solar panels on the roof Usually yes Debris under panels is hard to reach and guards reduce what gets up there
A fire risk area Yes, and specify ember guard mesh Ember protection is a different rating from leaf exclusion. Ask for it specifically
Box gutters on a commercial roof Case by case A blocked box gutter is a very expensive failure, but guard access can also make inspection harder

Swipe for the rest of the columns

Mesh types

Three choices and what separates them

Aluminium mesh

The common domestic choice. Durable, does not rust, available in Colorbond colours so it is close to invisible from the ground. Good leaf exclusion.

Steel and ember rated mesh

Specified for bushfire prone areas, where the mesh aperture and the material are both rated. If this is why you want guards, say so, because ordinary leaf mesh does not qualify.

Plastic and poly mesh

Cheapest, and it is cheap for a reason. It goes brittle in UV over a few Melbourne summers and then fails in sheets, usually into the gutter it was protecting.

Guards do not fix a gutter that is already failing

Fitting mesh over a rusted gutter, a run that has lost its fall or brackets that have dropped means paying to cover a problem rather than fix it. The gutter gets assessed first, and where it needs work we will say so rather than quoting mesh over the top of it.

Questions

Asked before fitting guards

Will I never have to clean my gutters again?

No, and anyone who says otherwise is selling. A guard stops the bulk material, which is most of the problem under trees. Fine debris still passes through, leaf still mats on top of the mesh, and the gutter still needs inspecting.

Realistically it takes a house from twice a year to every two or three years, and the visit becomes clearing the mesh rather than digging out the channel.

How much do gutter guards cost?

Per linear metre, fitted, with the mesh type and the roof profile setting the rate. A simple tile roof with straightforward access is at one end, a complex metal roof with valleys and a steep pitch at the other.

The useful comparison is against what you currently spend on cleaning. Under a gum, guards normally pay back in three to five years. On an open block they may never.

Do guards stop ember attack?

Only if the mesh is rated for it, and ordinary leaf mesh is not. Ember guard has a specified aperture and material, and it is a different product.

If bushfire protection is the reason you want guards, say so at quote stage so the right mesh is specified rather than the cheaper one.

Will a guard stop water getting into the gutter in heavy rain?

A well fitted one, no. A badly fitted one, yes, and it is the main failure mode. Mesh fitted too flat or without the right profile can cause water to run over the top of the gutter in a downpour, which is the exact problem it was bought to prevent.

It is a fitting issue rather than a product issue, and it is why the roof profile matters when quoting.

Can you clean gutters that already have guards?

Yes, and it is a different job from clearing an open gutter. Sections of mesh have to be lifted and refitted, which takes longer, and that is worth knowing when comparing the ongoing cost.

Mesh that has been crudely levered up and put back badly is a common find, so we are careful about how it goes back.
